host.name: ConfigButler
host.description: A managed configuration control plane: a typed, schema-validated realtime API for configuration, with every accepted change committed to the customer's own Git repository.

entries.description: What ConfigButler is: one managed control plane with two ways in (application configuration and GitOps), and how a request becomes a durable record in Git.
representativeQueries: managed configuration API backed by Git
configuration control plane for applications and agents

entries.description: Giving an application a typed configuration API — schemas, validation, realtime watches — without building and operating a configuration backend.
representativeQueries: typed runtime configuration API for my application
alternative to storing app settings in config files
schema-defined settings API with realtime updates

entries.description: A realtime API in front of an existing Git repository: people, services, and agents interact through an API instead of editing YAML, and writes become reviewable pull requests.
representativeQueries: API in front of a GitOps repository
let developers request infrastructure without editing YAML
self-service platform requests that become pull requests

entries.description: How it works: a managed Kubernetes-style control plane as the operational truth, continuously synchronized to a customer-owned Git repository as the durable source of record.
representativeQueries: Kubernetes-style control plane synchronized to Git
KRM API with Git as the source of record

entries.description: The technology developed in public behind ConfigButler: GitOps Reverser, KRM Stream, and the Reverse GitOps operating model.
